clue.text: Commonly, introductions to orgiastic films XX

indicators.note: the introductions to words are their opening letters, taken here from orgiastic and films

parts.note: read the Roman numerals as X (ten) followed by the multiplication sign x (times)

explanation.surface: Someone notes how often racy films open with an XX certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: XX looks like a film rating or twenty, but is read as two separate symbols: the Roman ten and the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean frequently or often, the answer being an old-fashioned adverb for the same idea.

clue.text: Hellish in Nunhead with untamed environment

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the wild word is put around the letter

parts.note: an untamed animal is feral, gone wild
read as Nun-head: the head (first letter) of Nun is N

explanation.surface: Nunhead, a London district, is described as hellish, with wild surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: Nunhead is a real district of south London; split it as the head of Nun to get N. 'environment' puts FERAL round that N.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal relates to the inferno, the underworld of fire, so it is a synonym of hellish.

clue.text: Reference book breaking rule remains to be edited

indicators.note: breaking into means the single letter is set inside the rearranged letters
text to be edited will be reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference book departs from the rules, and its remaining text still needs editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reference book' reads as one thing, a dictionary perhaps; split it, as 'book' only supplies a letter. 'to be edited' gives SERIALNUMER, and 'breaking' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial number is a unique identifying code, used as a reference for a manufactured item.

clue.text: See 10
Report still in the papers

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: still in the sense of motionless is stationary

explanation.surface: A news report is still running in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Still and papers are spelt differently but sound the same: stationary (not moving) and stationery (writing materials).
explanation.definitionFit: Stationery is writing materials, chiefly paper and envelopes, so papers stands for it.

clue.text: Mount starts to trouble rider in its seat

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the seat word

parts.note: a rider's seat on a horse is the saddle

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, here of trouble and rider

explanation.surface: A horse gives trouble to the rider sitting in its saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a horse is to sit astride it, which is what straddle means.

clue.text: Dangerous to cut wire, ultimately

parts.note: to sever is to cut through

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of wire

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal warning: cutting the wire is ultimately risky.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe illness or storm is serious and dangerous, a common synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Describing kiss in rising scream of passion?

definitions.text: Describing kiss in rising scream of passion?

indicators.note: in places the kiss letter inside the cry
in a down entry rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an ecstatic cry of yes
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Something describes a kiss amid a mounting cry of ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns YES into SEY, and 'in' puts X inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy describes something erotic, as a kiss inside a passionate yes would be.

clue.text: Criminal job — one's driven into the ground

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A criminal job, apparently ending with someone buried in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's driven into the ground' sounds like a buried victim of the crime, but it is a stake hammered in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence post is a stake hammered into the earth to hold up a fence.

clue.text: Before gravity, the elementary particle giving 3 20?

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the gravity letter

parts.note: taken as written
a meson is a subatomic particle
g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A physics puzzle about which particle comes before gravity, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 20' sends you to the linked answer SERIAL NUMBER: a number in a serial, like the tune played at the start of each episode.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial on TV or radio has its own signature tune, a number that recurs in every episode.

clue.text: Time when grand ancient city almost knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way, so the word is read backwards
almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Nineveh was an ancient city of Assyria
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An ancient city is nearly toppled by a grand event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the Assyrian capital, 'knocked over' reverses what is left, and G, slang for a grand, closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the time of day between afternoon and night.

clue.text: Essay about getting on — read it and weep!

indicators.note: about means the attempt word wraps round the age word

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try
someone getting on in years is aged

explanation.surface: An essay about ageing is so sad it brings tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a written piece but is the verb or noun meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a sad drama, the kind of story you read and weep over.

clue.text: Entering apartment on a landing using a key

indicators.note: the answer enters, sitting inside, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Getting into a flat on a landing by using a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using a key' sounds like a door key; it is the musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal music is written in a key, as opposed to atonal music.

clue.text: Lurid figure's incest most unclear?

annotationWithheld.why: Lurid figure's incest most unclear? (9): the only parse splits 'incest' as container word 'in' plus CEST, so the word 'incest' is both the insertion indicator and the fodder

clue.text: Helpful message about cigar butt I found in Panama

indicators.note: about means the message word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: found in places the letters inside the hat word

parts.note: a Panama is a type of straw hat

indicators.note: a cigar butt is its end, the last letter

explanation.surface: A helpful note concerns a cigar stub found in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' suggests the country but is the straw hat. 'butt' takes the end of cigar; 'found in' puts that plus I into the hat, and 'about' wraps the telegram word round the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means generous and kindly, so helpful is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Dangerous surges laid waste to fuse, with volts passing through

indicators.note: something passing through goes inside, so the letter is placed within
fused letters are melted together and reformed, rearranged

parts.note: V is the symbol for volts

explanation.surface: Electrical surges wreck everything, blowing a fuse as voltage passes through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid waste' reads as the surges' destruction, but it is the fodder; 'to fuse' rearranges it, and 'passing through' places V inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal waves are huge, destructive surges of sea water.

clue.text: Simply a wild animal in the grass? I can't tell

indicators.note: wild letters run free, so they are rearranged
in places the animal inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a seal is a marine animal

explanation.surface: Is a wild animal simply hiding in the grass? Someone refuses to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simply a wild' reads as describing the animal, but 'wild' rearranges the two words before it. 'in' sets the marine mammal inside the tall grass, giving RESEALED.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a promise to keep a secret, said by someone who will not tell.

clue.text: Little-brained philosopher's verbal diarrhoea exposed

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: diarrhoea is loose poo; something exposed is bare

explanation.surface: A thinker of little intelligence spouts nonsense, now laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie-the-Pooh calls himself a bear of very little brain, and his musings have been sold as philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's bear is famously of very little brain and dispenses homespun wisdom.

clue.text: Oil finally greases wheels, which is beneficial

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of oil
wheels turn, so the letters are rolled around into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil eventually greases the wheels, which helps everything run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like the noun being greased, but it is the anagram signal for GREASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, money or gifts that benefit the recipients.

clue.text: Importance that is with Tony Blair finally is in tatters

indicators.note: something in tatters is torn up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Blair

explanation.surface: A political comment: Tony Blair's standing is finally in shreds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tatters' rearranges IE, TONY, R (the end of Blair) and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniority is higher rank or status, a form of importance.

clue.text: See 3
Fairy lights initially bringing danger

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of lights

explanation.surface: Fairy lights at Christmas pose a fire hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy lights' reads as the Christmas decoration; split them. A PERI is a fairy of Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is a direct synonym for danger.

clue.text: Moon, showing bum in outskirts of Paris

indicators.note: in places the tramp word inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant, a hobo

explanation.surface: Someone moons, showing their bottom on the edge of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' and 'Moon' suggest showing a bottom; here bum is the American word for a tramp, and Moon the satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is the larger of the two moons of Mars.

clue.text: Nation at war one beginning to believe perfect, on reflection

parts.note: 'Nam is Vietnam, where America was at war
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the beginning of believe is its first letter
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is turned round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written as AI

explanation.surface: A nation at war is one that is starting to believe it is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns AI (A1, first-class) to IA. 'Nam is slang for Vietnam during its war.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a nation in south-west Africa.

clue.text: Twelve ducks in the news

indicators.note: in places the zeros inside the pair of letters

parts.note: news read as plural of new, N's: two Ns
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A dozen ducks appear in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nothing, so two ducks are OO. Read 'news' as two Ns, N being short for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock midday.

clue.text: State to arrest a disease

indicators.note: to state something is to say it aloud, so the words are heard

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to arrest them; a gives A

explanation.surface: The state moves to arrest the spread of a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation or condition, but it is the verb meaning say, so COLLAR A is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an infectious bacterial disease of the intestine.

clue.text: Solid figure supporting Conservative

indicators.note: in a down entry supporting means below, so the number goes under the party letter

parts.note: one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A firm figure backing the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a solid shape in geometry, tapering from a round base to a point.

clue.text: Classical character, round and huge

parts.note: O is round in shape
mega means huge

explanation.surface: A rotund and enormous figure from the classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical character' suggests a figure in Greek drama; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a classical letter.

clue.text: Seafood good to throw out into the road

indicators.note: into places the pieces inside the road word

parts.note: a lane is a road
to oust is to throw out

explanation.surface: Seafood that's off gets thrown into the street.
explanation.walkthrough: LANGOUSTE is the French name for the spiny lobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A langouste is a spiny lobster, eaten as seafood.
